summary: Returns the value after checking that it is not a number.
description: The test is `typeof value === "number"`, which `NaN` and both infinities satisfy. Use `isFloat`, `isInteger` or `isNaN` when those cases have to be told apart.
`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

params.message: The message of the exception. A default is used when omitted.
params.strict: When `true`, a string counts as empty only if it has no characters at all; by default whitespace is trimmed first.

returns: the same value, with a number excluded from its type.

examples.title: What passes and what does not
examples.body:
```javascript
requireNonNumber("1"); // => "1"
requireNonNumber(null); // => null
requireNonNumber(0); // throws IllegalArgumentException
requireNonNumber(1.5); // throws IllegalArgumentException
```
